posts.title: How I Found Myself Writing reverse-bin
posts.description: This is the backstory for reverse-bin: My Retro-Futuristic Successor to CGI-BIN . In the early 2000s Linux was cool, corporate types used Windows and kids were learning Linux. Linux systems were multi-user and ~/public_html was the way to publish a static website and one could do some backflips with apache config to get something similar for dynamic websites using PHP or general-purpose cgi-bin. c

posts.title: reverse-bin: My Retro-Futuristic Successor to CGI-BIN
posts.description: I feel that the modern way of hosting apps is too complex and the old cgi-bin way was also suboptimal. I kept the cgi-bin subprocess model and married it with reverse proxying in https://github.com/tarasglek/caddy-reverse-bin/ . posts.title: The Case for Secrets as Code: Stop Click-Managing Secrets
posts.description: We live in the age of software as a service, secret keys are everywhere. Yet somehow it is still normal to click-manage secrets. Smart people share them via signal,smarter people, share them via a password manager like Bitwarden.
